subtitle: UPDATE Jul 26, 2:12pm BRT, 70 days from the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). A Sunday with no new poll: the [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) of Jul 24 (n=2,004, fieldwork Jul 22 to 24, 2pp margin, BR-01166/2026) is still the most recent national survey, with Lula at 40% and Flávio at 32% in the first round and 48% x 43% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). The [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) register shows that changes on Monday: four national polls with publication declared within five days, [Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) on Jul 27, [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) on Jul 28 with n=5,000, PoderData on Jul 30 and Vox Brasil on Jul 31, three of them with fieldwork open right now and therefore measuring after the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention. In the market, the day was one of internal reshuffling: Lula stood EXACTLY still at 62.50%, which is the top of the AFOS series, while Flávio rose 0.80pp to 23.65% and Renan Santos fell exactly 0.80pp to 9.55%. A move of the same size and opposite sign between two names in the same camp, with the front-runner motionless, describes a dispute WITHIN a camp and not a transfer between camps. The gap pulled back to +38.85pp, off the peak of +39.65pp recorded yesterday. The fact of the day was the PSD national convention, which made Ronaldo Caiado its presidential candidate with Gilberto Kassab as running mate, and whose price in the book FELL 0.15pp, to 1.75%, in the same session. It is the second launch in a row ending down, after Flávio fell 0.10pp the day before, and in both cases the coincidence is recorded without any claim of causation. On the institutional front, the escalation with Argentina advanced: after Javier Milei’s attack on Alexandre de Moraes from a Brazilian stage, the president of the [STF](/en/glossary#stf), Edson Fachin, answered publicly and the government summoned its ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 115.95M. Cross-reference with live [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) Jul 26, 17:12 UTC, approved by a double reading with an 8 minute interval.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: Polymarket 62.50% (flat, vol USD 7.65M accumulated), 70 days from the election. He stood exactly still at the top of the AFOS series, a level he reached on Jul 25 and that no earlier day had touched. The gap over Flávio pulled back to +38.85pp, below the peak of +39.65pp of the day before. In polling, the Datafolha of Jul 24 is still the reference, with 40% in the first round and 48% in the head-to-head runoff against Flávio’s 43%.
fortes: He held the top of the series without giving anything back: 62.50% for a second day, with accumulated volume of USD 7.65M.
The day’s movement happened entirely between the second and third placed names, without touching his price, which points to an internal dispute in the opposing camp.
The Datafolha of Jul 24 keeps him ahead in all three runoff scenarios tested: 48% x 43% against Flávio, 47% x 40% against Caiado and 48% x 40% against Zema.
The launch of a third competitive candidate, Caiado for the PSD, produced no transfer of price against him: what gave way in the book was the chasing pack itself.
Personal approval of 49% against 48% disapproval in the most recent read, with the two ends swapping places compared with June.
fracos: The gap pulled back 0.80pp and came off the previous day’s peak, meaning yesterday’s record lasted one day.
There was no new poll to test the 62.50% level, and the distance between price and declared vote has had no fresh measurement since Jul 24.
The assessment of the ADMINISTRATION remains negative and is a different question from personal approval: 38% bad or terrible against 32% great or good.
The swap between approval and disapproval is 1pp in a survey with a 2pp margin, which is a statistical tie and not a reversal.
The week brings four national polls in five days, three with fieldwork after the PL convention, which means the current level goes into immediate testing.
candidates.analise: His Sunday was one of complete immobility, and that is more informative than it looks. The price stayed at 62.50%, exactly where it closed the day before, over a weekend that had the launch convention of a third candidate, diplomatic escalation with Argentina and a public reply from the president of the STF to a foreign head of state. None of that moved the front-runner. All the movement in the book happened between Flávio, who rose 0.80pp, and Renan Santos, who fell exactly 0.80pp, which is the typical shape of reallocation within a camp and not of a transfer between camps. The gap pulled back to +38.85pp and came off the peak of +39.65pp of the day before, which needs to be said as clearly as the record was recorded: the top lasted one session. In polling there was no news, and the Datafolha of Jul 24 (n=2,004, fieldwork Jul 22 to 24, 2pp margin, BR-01166/2026) remains the heaviest read, with 40% in the first round, 48% in the runoff against Flávio and personal approval of 49% against 48%. The test arrives fast: the TSE register shows four national polls with publication declared between Jul 27 and Jul 31, with the AtlasIntel of Jul 28 the largest in sample, at n=5,000, and the first big one whose fieldwork sits entirely after the PL convention. His accumulated volume at USD 7.65M, in a presidential market adding up to USD 115.95M.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: Polymarket 23.65% (up 0.80pp, vol USD 7.67M accumulated), one day after the convention that made his candidacy official. He recovered the ground lost on the day of the launch itself and moved away from the 22.00% floor the series records on Jul 3. He consolidated second place in the first round at 78.00%, up 1.50pp. In polling, the Datafolha of Jul 24 puts him at 32% in the first round and 43% in the head-to-head runoff against Lula’s 48%.
fortes: Largest rise in the book on the day: up 0.80pp to 23.65%, comfortably recovering the 0.10pp fall recorded on the day of his own convention.
He consolidated second place in the first round at 78.00%, up 1.50pp, which reinforces the reading that he is the one who reaches the runoff if there is one.
His rise mirrors exactly Renan Santos’ fall, which indicates the market sees him picking up his competitor’s space within the same camp.
The Datafolha of Jul 24 records him at 32% in the first round, one point above June, and keeps the 43% of the head-to-head runoff.
The candidacy has been formalised since Jul 25, which closes the pre-candidacy phase and frees up the campaign calendar.
fracos: The rise came one day AFTER the event, which weakens any reading that the market took the convention as a gain.
The gain has an identifiable origin inside his own camp: Renan gave up 0.80pp, exactly what he rose, and Lula did not move. There was no advance on the front-runner.
Rejection remains the ceiling: 48% in the Datafolha of Jul 24, identical to June and the highest among all names tested.
The surrounding family names retreated on the same day: Jair fell 0.20pp to 1.05% and Michelle fell 0.40pp to 0.75%, dropping out of the 1% range.
He still has no running mate after Tereza Cristina’s refusal, and her price in the presidential book remains at 0.15%, with conventions running through Aug 5.
candidates.analise: He had the largest rise of the day and its origin is the data point that matters. He rose 0.80pp to 23.65% (vol USD 7.67M), comfortably recovering the 0.10pp fall he had recorded on the day of the convention itself. But Renan Santos fell exactly 0.80pp in the same session, and Lula did not move a hundredth. When two names in the same camp trade the same amount of price between them and the front-runner stands still, what you are seeing is internal consolidation, not an advance on the opponent. It is good news for him and it is smaller news than the size of the number suggests. In the first-round second place market the move went the same way and was stronger, up 1.50pp to 78.00%, although that book is worth USD 4.27M against the USD 7.67M of his main price. The timing also deserves an honest record: the rise came one day after the convention, not on the day of it, which makes it hard to sustain that the market read the event as a gain. In polling nothing changed, because there was no new survey, and the Datafolha of Jul 24 still shows his structural problem intact: a 48% rejection rate, the highest in the race, without a single digit of variation against June. And the surrounding names retreated on the very day he rose, with Jair giving up 0.20pp and Michelle 0.40pp, which is consistent with a market consolidating around a single name in the camp.

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: Polymarket 9.55% in the winner market (down 0.80pp, vol USD 8.53M accumulated), the largest fall in the book on the day and a second consecutive session of losses. He also lost 1.50pp in the first-round third place market, going to 64.50%. The most recent poll, the Datafolha of Jul 24, measures him at 3% in the first round, which puts three of the four recent national surveys at that level.
fortes: He keeps the third highest price in the presidential book and the largest accumulated volume among the competitive names, USD 8.53M, above Lula and Flávio.
He remains dominant in the first-round third place market, at 64.50%, far ahead of the runner-up there, Caiado at 15.50%.
He rose 0.10pp in the first-round second place market, to 11.85%, keeping the runoff hypothesis alive despite the fall in his main price.
His rejection in the Datafolha is 12%, a quarter of Flávio's, which preserves room to grow that the top two candidates do not have.
fracos: Second consecutive day of losses: he lost 1.40pp the day before and another 0.80pp today, going from 11.75% to 9.55% in two sessions.
He lost the 10% handle and gave up 1.50pp in the first-round third place market, meaning the loss was not confined to the winner contract.
Today’s fall has an exact counterpart in Flávio’s rise, which describes a market reallocating within the camp and picking the other name.
The distortion against polling is still the widest on the panel, 9.55% of price against 3% of declared vote, even though it narrowed through movement in the price.
Measured against the whole series, 9.55% is well below the peak of 17.90% on Jun 9, so the current level is a retreat from a level already lost.
candidates.analise: It was the second consecutive session of losses and, taken together, the two draw a consistent move: he fell 1.40pp the day before, when the Datafolha measured him at 3%, and another 0.80pp today, going from 11.75% to 9.55% in two days. The detail that gives today’s fall its meaning is the counterpart: Flávio rose exactly 0.80pp in the same session, and Lula did not move. It is not his camp shrinking against the front-runner, it is the market picking another name inside the same camp. That gains context from the political reading that circulated over the weekend, that the PT sees Renan as a direct threat to Flávio and not to Lula, but AFOS records the coincidence of framing and does not assert that one thing caused the other. The loss did not stay in the winner contract: he gave up 1.50pp in the first-round third place market, to 64.50%, and gained only 0.10pp in second place, to 11.85%. On the distortion the panel tracks, it went on narrowing by the same mechanism as yesterday, that is, through the PRICE and not the polls: 9.55% of implied probability against 3% of declared vote in the three converging national surveys. It is still the widest distance on the panel and it is still a comparison between different quantities, probability of victory against voting intention. Series caveat: 9.55% is neither a high nor a low for him, with a peak of 17.90% on Jun 9 and a floor of 5.30% on Apr 26. He holds the largest accumulated volume among the competitive names, USD 8.53M, which measures traded history and not current conviction.

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: Polymarket: Caiado 1.75% (down 0.15pp, vol USD 5.14M), Jair 1.05% (down 0.20pp, vol USD 5.24M), Michelle 0.75% (down 0.40pp, vol USD 9.26M), Zema 0.65% (down 0.10pp, vol USD 4.53M), Camilo Santana 0.45%, Haddad 0.35% (down 0.30pp, vol USD 6.36M), Alckmin 0.25%, Tarcísio 0.15%. In the Datafolha of Jul 24, Caiado has 4%, Zema 3% and both lose the runoff to Lula, 47x40 and 48x40.
candidates.subtitle: Jul 26, 70 days out: the chasing pack had its busiest day on the calendar and its quietest day in price. The PSD made Ronaldo Caiado its presidential candidate with Gilberto Kassab as running mate, in a national convention, and in his first speech as a candidate he attacked both front-runners, saying that Lula provokes Trump and that Flávio attacks public authorities (Folha de S.Paulo, G1, Times Brasil). In the book, ALL the names in the pack retreated: Caiado 0.15pp to 1.75%, Jair 0.20pp to 1.05%, Michelle 0.40pp to 0.75%, Zema 0.10pp to 0.65% and Haddad 0.30pp to 0.35%. The money that left the pack and Renan Santos showed up in a single place, which was Flávio.

caiado.label: CAIADO (PSD), presidential Poly 1.75% (down 0.15pp, vol USD 5.14M) | first-round third place 15.50% (down 0.50pp) | MADE OFFICIAL as candidate at the PSD national convention on Jul 26, with Kassab as running mate | Datafolha Jul 24 first round 4% and runoff Lula 47% x Caiado 40%, rejection 12%
caiado.fortes: He went from pre-candidate to candidate: the PSD national convention made the ticket official on Jul 26, with Gilberto Kassab as running mate, a ticket built entirely within the party and with no need for a federation. He is the best measured name in the pack in the Datafolha of Jul 24, at 4% in the first round, and has one of the lowest rejection rates in the race, 12%, against Flávio’s 48% and Lula’s 46%. That room to grow is what the market prices when it keeps him alive despite the low declared vote. In his first speech as a candidate he aimed at both front-runners at once, trying to occupy the space between them.
caiado.fracos: The price FELL on the very day of the convention that made him official, 0.15pp to 1.75%, and gave up another 0.50pp in the first-round third place market, going to 15.50%. It is the second launch in a row on the calendar in which the candidate being made official ends the session down. The Datafolha dismantled the competitive runoff thesis: Lula beats him 47% to 40%, seven points, a margin WIDER than the five points against Flávio. He measures 4% of declared vote and is worth 1.75% in the winner book, a contrast that persists with no sign of correction.

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), presidential Poly 0.35% (down 0.30pp, vol USD 6.36M) | not tested for president by any national poll, including the Datafolha of Jul 24 | focus on the São Paulo state race, with the ticket made official on Jul 25 and Márcio França (PSB) as running mate
haddad.fortes: He remains the PT’s leading figure in the country’s largest electorate, with the São Paulo state ticket made official at a convention in Campinas on Jul 25, with Márcio França as running mate and Lula present, which closed months of negotiation.
haddad.fracos: He gave back the previous day’s rise in full and then some: down 0.30pp to 0.35%, dropping out of the half-point range. Yesterday’s read already recorded that the rise coincided with a STATE convention and that the office priced in the book is a different one; giving it back the next day is consistent with that. No national poll tests him for president, including the Datafolha of Jul 24, so his price is residue of a well-known name with no polling backing in the office being priced.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), presidential Poly 0.65% (down 0.10pp, vol USD 4.53M) | first-round third place 4.75% | Datafolha Jul 24 first round 3% and runoff Lula 48% x Zema 40%, rejection 13% | still with NO running mate announced, with conventions through Aug 5
zema.fortes: He keeps a low rejection rate by the standards of this race, 13% in the Datafolha of Jul 24, in a field where the two front-runners are above 45%. He marks 3% consistently in the recent national polls (Datafolha, Gerp and Indexa), plus 3.7% in Futura/Apex of Jul 14 and 4% in BTG/Nexus of Jul 13, meaning the level is stable and not erratic.
zema.fracos: Third session of retreat in four days: he fell another 0.10pp and reached 0.65%, his lowest level since the jump of Jul 24. In the Datafolha he loses the runoff to Lula 48% to 40%, the widest margin among the three runoff scenarios tested, and his 13% rejection rate is the highest in the pack. He still has no running mate announced while the convention calendar runs through Aug 5, and now with a direct competitor in the same space already made official, which shortens the time he has to differentiate himself.

candidates.analise: The chasing pack lived the paradox of the day: it had the fullest calendar and the weakest price. The PSD made Caiado its presidential candidate with Kassab as running mate, a ticket built entirely within the party, at a national convention, and in his first speech as a candidate he attacked Lula and Flávio at the same time, trying to occupy the space between the two (Folha de S.Paulo, G1, Times Brasil, Jul 26). The market answered with a fall of 0.15pp, to 1.75%, and also cut 0.50pp from his position in the first-round third place market. And it was not only him: ALL the names in the pack retreated in the same session, with Jair giving up 0.20pp, Michelle 0.40pp, Zema 0.10pp and Haddad 0.30pp. The money that left the pack and Renan Santos showed up in a single place, which was Flávio, up 0.80pp. The reading the data supports is one of consolidation: the market is concentrating the non-government camp in a single name, and it did so on the very day a competitor was formally launched. On polling, nothing changed, and the Datafolha of Jul 24 remains the measured ceiling of the pack, with Caiado at 4%, Zema at 3% and Augusto Cury at 2%, plus runoffs in which Lula beats Caiado 47% to 40% and Zema 48% to 40%, margins wider than the 5pp against Flávio. The honest counterpoint is still rejection: Caiado 12% and Zema 13%, against Flávio’s 48% and Lula’s 46%, meaning they have room to grow that the top two do not. The usual methodological caveat applies: these are prices between 0.35% and 1.75% in a book where the front-runner is worth 62.50%, so variation in percentage points looks large in relative terms and is small in money.
fortes: Caiado is no longer a pre-candidate: the PSD national convention made the ticket official with Kassab as running mate on Jul 26, with no need for a federation.
Caiado is the best measured name in the pack in the Datafolha, at 4% in the first round, and has one of the lowest rejection rates in the race, 12%.
Zema keeps rejection low, 13% in the Datafolha, in a field where the top two candidates are above 45%.
Renan Santos, despite the fall, remains dominant in the first-round third place market, at 64.50% against Caiado’s 15.50%.
fracos: ALL the names in the pack retreated in the same session, and the money showed up concentrated in a single name, which was Flávio.
Caiado fell 0.15pp on the very day of the convention that made him official, and lost another 0.50pp in the first-round third place market.
Haddad gave back the previous day’s rise in full, falling 0.30pp to 0.35%, which confirms that the rise was noise from a state convention.
Michelle fell 0.40pp and dropped out of the 1% range, despite still holding the largest accumulated volume in the book among the names that are not Tarcísio.
None of them goes above 4% in the Datafolha, and the two tested in the runoff lose by 7pp and 8pp, margins wider than Flávio’s.

cruzamento: Jul 26 was a Sunday of a full calendar, empty polling and a market reshuffling internally. Start with what did NOT happen: no new national poll was published, and the Datafolha of Jul 24 (n=2,004, fieldwork Jul 22 to 24, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-01166/2026) remains the heaviest read, with Lula at 40% and Flávio at 32% in the first round and 48% x 43% in the head-to-head runoff. That changes immediately: the TSE register shows four national polls with publication declared within five days, Nexus on Jul 27 with n=2,000, AtlasIntel on Jul 28 with n=5,000, PoderData on Jul 30 with n=2,400 and Vox Brasil on Jul 31 with n=2,100. Three of them have fieldwork open at this moment, which means they will be the first to measure the electorate after the PL convention. A methodological caveat applies: those dates are what each institute declared to the TSE when filing the survey, and a filing is not a publication. Now the market, and here is the finding of the day. Lula stood EXACTLY still at 62.50% (vol USD 7.65M), holding the top of the AFOS series for a second session. Flávio rose 0.80pp to 23.65% (vol USD 7.67M) and Renan Santos fell exactly 0.80pp to 9.55% (vol USD 8.53M). Two names in the same camp trading the same amount of price between them, with the front-runner motionless, is the shape of a dispute WITHIN a camp, not of a transfer between camps. The gap pulled back to +38.85pp and came off the peak of +39.65pp recorded yesterday, and this needs to be said as clearly as the record was announced: the top lasted one session. The third element is the political fact of the day, and it produced the most interesting cross-reference. The PSD national convention made Ronaldo Caiado its presidential candidate with Gilberto Kassab as running mate, a ticket built entirely within the party, and in his first speech as a candidate he attacked both front-runners at once, saying that Lula provokes Trump and that Flávio attacks public authorities (Folha de S.Paulo, G1, Times Brasil, Jul 26). His price FELL 0.15pp in the same session, to 1.75%, and he also lost 0.50pp in the first-round third place market. It is the second launch in a row in which this happens, because Flávio also fell, by 0.10pp, on the day of his own convention. Two occurrences do not make a pattern and causation is asserted in neither: these are small books and single-instant captures. But the record is honest and worth tracking through the remaining conventions, up to Aug 5. Add to that the behaviour of the whole chasing pack: ALL of them retreated in the same session, Caiado 0.15pp, Jair 0.20pp, Michelle 0.40pp, Zema 0.10pp and Haddad 0.30pp, and the money showed up concentrated in a single name. What the data describes is a market consolidating the non-government camp in Flávio, on the very day a competitor was formally launched. The fourth axis is institutional and escalated in three stages over the weekend, with no price counterpart at all. After Javier Milei called Alexandre de Moraes a bald piece of trash from the stage of the PL convention, the president of the STF, Edson Fachin, replied publicly that the remark is incompatible with civility (G1, Estadão, Folha de S.Paulo, Jul 25). Next, the American government denied any intention of undermining elections in Brazil, responding to the visa refusal by Itamaraty (Folha de S.Paulo, Jul 25). And this Sunday the Brazilian government summoned its ambassador in Argentina for consultations (Folha de S.Paulo, Jul 26). The market on the impeachment of a STF justice stood at 3.40%, down 0.10pp, effectively flat for the third day, in a book of USD 83 thousand that supports no narrative whatsoever. A contrast of scale the panel keeps in view: in the Senate seats market the PL swung between 69% and 70% within the capture window itself, a move of 1pp in thirteen minutes in a book adding up to USD 292 thousand. That instability is, in itself, the argument for not building a reading on that market. One final collection caveat, because omitting it would be worse than recording it: the news query on the Master case returned ZERO items today, which may be a short window or aggregator blocking. The panel kept the previous picture of the case instead of declaring an empty day, because absence of search results is not evidence of absence of facts. The synthesis, with no value judgement: the polls did not speak, the market did not change its mind about who wins and spent Sunday deciding who loses better, and the week ahead brings four measurements to test both.
